title: Performance — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: One of the most complete and rigorous planes in the library — P0–P11 all shipped, 366 assertions — and it does what OpenTelemetry and Prometheus split across separate tools: it closes the OTel triad (metrics + traces + logs, all in native OTLP JSON) and exposes Prometheus text, and adds SLA judgment with edge-triggered alerting, a sampling profiler, queueing-theory capacity analysis (utilization & Little's law, each with an independent self-check), and a driven-load harness — one coherent plane. Its real signature is measurement discipline: clocks as scopes, Windows 15.6 ms quantization handled, self-cost priced with its own machinery, and a rule that unmeasured is an error, never a silent pass. What it is not, by design, is the storage-and-dashboard half.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Against OTel (an instrumentation SDK) and Prometheus (storage + alerting), this is one plane doing the instrumentation, the analysis, and the judgment — and leaving storage to the scraper.

lanes.engine: Counters / gauges / timers (`stzMetric`) and Prometheus-style labeled families (`stzMetricFamily`) with the child registry engine-side (`perf.zig Family`) so children are visible across all Ring faces, and cardinality bounded at birth with a reserved, counted overflow child.
lanes.owed: At parity — full metric types, labels, and bounded cardinality that never silently drops. The overflow child is the honest touch most clients lack.

lanes.engine: Two independent engines: an O(1) log-bucket sketch (`histogram.zig`, 16 fixed ms bounds + overflow) and a sort-exact nearest-rank over the retained window (`perf_series_percentile`) — plus `histogram_sum` keeping an exact lifetime sum while the buckets quantize, so the mean is exact.
lanes.owed: Exact and sketch, both labeled by kind at the call site — ahead of Prometheus's bucket-only summaries. Nothing structural owed.

lanes.engine: Both worlds, all three signals: Prometheus text (`PromText`, label-aware) and OTLP JSON for metrics (`OtelJson`), spans (`stzOtelBatch`) and logs (`stzLog.OtelJson`). Built-in `GET /metrics` + `/health`; pull (scrape) and push (OTLP) both present.
lanes.owed: Broad exposition across both ecosystems and all three OTel signals. The storage/query side it deliberately leaves to the scraper (lane 12).

lanes.engine: `stzSla` (`ExpectP95(...).Under(...)`, warnings, `CheckAgainst`) emits verdicts in the unified rule shape into `stzRuleReport` (subject `perf`); `stzPerfSentinel` is edge-triggered (`OnBreach`/`OnClear`, event-bus fanout, a flight-recorder black box). NOT-MEASURED is an error, never a silent pass.
lanes.owed: SLA + alerting integrated into the same plane and the one CI gate — OTel has no alerting at all, and Prometheus's is a separate service. A distinctive, coherent lane.

lanes.engine: The plane's signature: clocks as scopes (monotonic `watch.zig` for durations, epoch wall kept separate), Windows 15.6 ms quantization handled (a "15.63 ms" read is one tick), `SelfCost()` priced with its own machinery (~0.03 ms), exact-transfer proven against frozen stubs, and the self-check identity law — a real check compares two independent measurements.
lanes.owed: Category-leading rigor — the transferable laws (leave-one-out z, the f64 2⁷³ serialization boundary, guard-honesty for live values) are arguably the plane's most valuable export.

lanes.engine: `stzPerfProfile`: utilization, throughput, response time, service demand, `MaxThroughput`, `Headroom`, a computing/waiting `Bottleneck` split, `MemoryTrendPerHour` / `HoursToMemoryCeiling`, and Little's law with an independent counted-in-flight self-check.
lanes.owed: Operational queueing-theory analysis neither OTel nor Prometheus offers — utilization and Little's law checked against a second, independent measurement, not asserted as an identity.

lanes.engine: Real W3C traceparent spans: parent→child join, an engine trace ring, and OTLP `resourceSpans` export (`stzOtelBatch`) that a Jaeger/Tempo collector reassembles. Every observed request gets a trace identity and echoes the header.
lanes.owed: Propagation is at the HTTP seam only — no baggage, no async-context through reactor jobs — a single global trace scope, and drop-oldest ring sampling rather than OTel head/tail. Below OTel's full context propagation.

lanes.engine: Inside a trace scope (`stzTraceScope`), every `stzLog` record stamps a queryable `traceId`; `OfTrace(id)` recovers a trip's log lines and `OtelJson` ships OTLP logs with traceId first-class — closing the third leg of the triad.
lanes.owed: One global scope slot — correct for one-request-per-loop, but parallel in-process dispatch would need per-task scopes (the same limit as tracing).

lanes.engine: `Observe` / `ObserveRoutes` wrap the appserver request seam, recording the well-known subjects (`http.request.ms`, `http.requests`, `http.errors`, `http.route.ms`), and `stzStopwatch` brackets any operation.
lanes.owed: Instrumentation is manual (you call `Observe`) — no auto-instrumentation of frameworks the way OTel agents wrap a server, client and DB without code changes.

lanes.engine: `stzProfiler` over an engine frame stack (per-path calls / total-ns / self-ns) and a real engine sampler thread photographing the active path, with folded (flamegraph-ready) output (`WriteFoldedTo`) and self-cost pricing.
lanes.owed: Frames are cooperative (Enter/Leave), not native-stack unwinding — depth-capped and bounded-path — so it profiles instrumented code, not an arbitrary un-instrumented call tree.

lanes.engine: `stzPerfPlan` — a closed catalog of optimization actions an LLM may propose but only an effectful actor may `ExecuteOn` (audited); and `stzLoadDriver` — a real driven-load harness (target + driver child processes, client-observed R, engine-exact percentiles).
lanes.owed: A distinctive pair — governed tuning + an in-library load generator that measured X sub-linear and R super-linear on a real fleet — but narrower than a dedicated load tool's scripting/scenarios.

lanes.engine: Bounded in-memory rings hold the recent window; everything is exposed and exported for a scraper or collector to store.
lanes.owed: No time-series database, no PromQL, no dashboards — export-only by explicit design. The half of "Prometheus" that stores and queries history, and the Grafana layer that draws it, are deliberately out of scope.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first closes the two OTel-ergonomics gaps; the second sharpens sampling, profiling and in-process aggregation; the third bridges to the storage/dashboard world it leaves to others.

items.title: Auto-instrumentation
items.text: Wrap the appserver, reactor client, backends and DB so metrics and traces appear without a manual `Observe` call — the "zero-code" value OTel agents provide. The seams already exist; this is making them opt-out rather than opt-in.

items.title: Full trace-context propagation
items.text: Baggage, async-context through reactor jobs, and per-task trace scopes — lifting the single-global-scope limit so a trace survives an async hop and a concurrent request keeps its own log stamps.

tiers.title: Tier B — sharpen sampling, profiling, aggregation

items.title: Head / tail trace sampling
items.text: Replace drop-oldest ring retention with head/tail sampling (keep the interesting traces — errors, slow tails) the way OTel does, so the exported spans are the ones worth reassembling.

items.title: In-process aggregation (PromQL-lite)
items.text: Rate/sum/quantile-over-children aggregation before the scrape, so a labeled family answers "p95 across all routes" without a PromQL server — a small analytic layer over the family store.

items.title: Native-stack profiling
items.text: Real stack unwinding alongside the cooperative frames, so un-instrumented code (and engine internals) show up in the flamegraph, not just `Enter`/`Leave` paths.

tiers.title: Tier C — bridge to storage & the platform gaps

items.title: A storage / dashboard integration story
items.text: A documented, tested path to Prometheus + Grafana (or an embedded lightweight TSDB) so the export-only design has a first-class "and here's how you keep and see the history" answer.

items.title: Engine-heap allocation stats
items.text: The deferred counting-allocator project — per-module engine-heap statistics beyond RSS/peak/trend, for when the operational question becomes "which module is allocating."

items.title: Close the platform gaps
items.text: macOS RSS (returns `-1`), and refresh the one stale metadata line — the CLAUDE.md perf-laws header still says "P0–P7 / 8 guards / 283 assertions" while the code is P0–P11 / 12 guards / 366.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Re-surveyed from `main`. Genuinely complete — every P0–P11 identifier resolves to real code — and rigorously guarded: 366 assertions across 12 guards plus ~22 engine `zig test` blocks, proving exact-transfer via frozen stubs, live-value ranges (not equalities, because live ratios drift both ways), and the self-check identity law (Little's implied N vs a counted in-flight; anchor-computed U vs a sampled gauge). The measurement laws are the transferable product. One stale metadata line noted above (the laws list itself is current); deliberate scope: export-only, HTTP-seam trace propagation, cooperative profiler frames, macOS RSS.

Softanza's performance plane is a single coherent system that closes the OpenTelemetry triad, exposes to Prometheus, and adds the SLA judgment, capacity analysis and load testing those tools leave to others — held to a measurement rigor most SDKs don't reach; its one deliberate boundary is that it instruments and analyses but does not store, query or draw.
